p: "שָׁלוֹם עֲלֵיכֶם מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת מַלְאֲכֵי עֶלְיוֹן... בּוֹאֲכֶם לְשָׁלוֹם מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁלוֹם
". "Peace be upon you, ministering angels, angels of the Most High... May your coming be in peace, angels of peace (mal'akhei ha-shalom)."
נִקְרְאוּ בְּכָאן הַמַּלְאָכִים בְּשֵׁם "מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁלוֹם
", Here in the Friday night liturgy, the angels are called by the name "angels of peace."
דְּשֵׁם "מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת" מוּבָן שֶׁהֵם מְשָׁרְתֵי ה' וּמְשַׁמְּשָׁיו
, Now the title "ministering angels" (mal'akhei ha-sharet) is readily understood, as they are the ministers and attendants of Hashem;
אֲבָל לְשׁוֹן "מַלְאֲכֵי שָׁלוֹם" מָצִינוּ רַק בַּחוּרְבָּן: "הֵן אֶרְאֶלָּם צָעֲקוּ חֻצָה מַלְאֲכֵי שָׁלוֹם מַר יִבְכָּיוּן" (יְשַׁעְיָה לג, ז
), yet the expression "angels of peace" is found in Scripture only regarding the Destruction: "Behold, their valiant ones cry without; the angels of peace weep bitterly" (Isaiah 33:7),
וּבַגְּמָרָא (חֲגִיגָה ה:): "שָׁאנֵי חוּרְבַּן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ דַּאֲפִילּוּ מַלְאֲכֵי שָׁלוֹם בָּכוּ
". and in the Gemara (Chagigah 5b): "The destruction of the Holy Temple is different, for even the angels of peace wept."
וְגַם שָׁם צָרִיךְ לְהָבִין מַה שֶּׁדִּקְדְּקוּ "אֲפִילּוּ מַלְאֲכֵי שָׁלוֹם", וְהָיָה לוֹ לוֹמַר דַּאֲפִילּוּ מַלְאָכִים בָּכוּ
; There too we must understand why the Gemara specified "even the angels of peace," when it could simply have said "even the angels wept";
וְכֵן יֵשׁ לְהָבִין לָמָּה קוֹרְאִין בְּלֵיל שַׁבָּת הַמַּלְאָכִים בְּשֵׁם "מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁלוֹם
". and similarly we must understand why on Sabbath eve we address the angels specifically as "angels of peace."

paragraphs.text: Ketubot 75a:14: “§ Since the Gemara quoted a statement of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi’s grandson, the Gemara cites another exposition in his name. p: וְזֶהוּ שֶׁאָמַר בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ: "וּבְגִינֵיהּ דְּיַעֲקֹב אַבְטַח לוֹן שְׁלִימוּ קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וְכוּלֵי, אִלֵּין אִקְרוּן מַלְאֲכֵי שָׁלוֹם
", And this is what the holy Zohar meant: "And for Jacob's sake the Holy One, blessed be He, promised them perfection (shelimu)... these are called the angels of peace,"
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁנִּקְרְאוּ כֵּן עַל שֵׁם שְׁלִימוּ דְּאַבְטַח לוֹן קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא בְּגִינֵיהּ דְּיַעֲקֹב
. meaning they were named thus after the perfection (shelimu / shalom) that the Holy One, blessed be He, promised them through Jacob.
וְהוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ סוֹף פָּרָשַׁת וַיֵּצֵא קסה עַמּוּד ב
): And this is further illuminated by what is written (in the holy Zohar at the end of Parashat Vayetzei, 165b): "
הַשְׁתָּא אִינּוּן 'וַיִּפְגְּעוּ בוֹ', בְּגִין דִּבְגִינֵיהּ דְּיַעֲקֹב וּבְאִינּוּן שִׁבְטִין אִתְשַׁקְיָין אִינּוּן מִמַּיָּא דְּיַמָּא רַבָּא", עַיֵּין שָׁם
. "Now it says of these angels 'and they met him,' because for the sake of Jacob and those twelve tribes, these angels are given to drink from the waters of the Great Sea," see there.
וְהַיְינוּ דְּמַיִם הוּא תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁנִּמְשַׁל לְמַיִם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "הוֹי כָּל צָמֵא לְכוּ לַמַּיִם" (יְשַׁעְיָה נה, א
), For the "waters of the Great Sea (Malchut)" refers to the Oral Torah, which is compared to water, as it is stated: "Ho, everyone who thirsts, come to the waters" (Isaiah 55:1),
וְנִדְרַשׁ (תַּעֲנִית ז.) עַל תַּלְמִיד חָכָם, עַיֵּין שָׁם, וְהַיְינוּ בְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
; which is expounded (Ta'anit 7a) regarding how a student must study from a master, see there, which pertains specifically to the Oral Torah;
וְזֶה נִמְשַׁל לְמַיִם שֶׁמַּנִּיחִין מָקוֹם גָּבוֹהַּ וְהוֹלְכִין לְמָקוֹם נָמוּךְ
, for it is the Oral Torah that is compared to water which leaves a high place and flows down to a low place,
דְּאִלּוּ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב כְּרוּכָה וּמוּנַּחַת בְּקֶרֶן זָוִית, כָּל הָרוֹצֶה יָבוֹא וְיִלְמוֹד, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (קִדּוּשִׁין סו
.). whereas the Written Torah lies rolled up and set in a corner, so that anyone who wishes may come and read it on his own, as they stated (Kiddushin 66a).
וְכֵן נִמְשְׁלָה הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה בְּאוֹתוֹ פָּסוּק לְיַיִן וְחָלָב ("לְכוּ שִׁבְרוּ בְּלוֹא כֶסֶף וּבְלוֹא מְחִיר יַיִן וְחָלָב
"), And in that same verse the Oral Torah is likewise compared to wine and milk ("buy wine and milk without money and without price"),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג רעא עַמּוּד ב): "בְּיֵינִי מָסַכְתִּי" – יֵינָא דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא דִּבְעַל פֶּה
. as is written (Zohar Part III, 271b) on "I have mingled my wine" (Proverbs 9:2) – this is the wine of the Oral Torah.
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁאָמַר דִּ"בְגִינֵיהּ דְּיַעֲקֹב וּבְאִינּוּן שִׁבְטִין" – שֶׁהַשְּׁבָטִים כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, מַלְכוּת פֶּה, תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
, And this is why the Zohar states "for the sake of Jacob and those tribes" – because the twelve tribes constitute Knesset Yisrael, Malchut ("the mouth," the Oral Torah),
וְיַעֲקֹב מַמְשִׁיךְ מִכֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן מִטַּלָּא דְּעַתִּיקָא לְמִדָּה זוֹ – "אִתְשַׁקְיָין וְכוּלֵי
", and Jacob channels from Keter Elyon, from the dew of Atika, into this attribute of the Great Sea – "they are given to drink, etc.,"
וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ דַּאֲכִילַת הַמַּלְאָכִים מִסִּטְרָא דְּאַבְרָהָם, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ קד עַמּוּד א): "דְּהָא מֵהַהוּא סִטְרָא נָפִיק מְזוֹנָא לְכֻלְּהוּ מַלְאֲכֵי עִלָּאֵי

", meaning that just as the spiritual "food" of the supernal angels emanates from the side of Abraham (Chesed), as written (in the holy Zohar, Vayera 104a): "For from that side emerges nourishment for all the supernal angels,"
כְּמוֹ כֵן בְּגִינֵיהּ דְּיַעֲקֹב אִתְשַׁקְיָין הַמַּלְאָכִים מִמַּיָּא דְּיַמָּא רַבָּא, וְהַיְינוּ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
, so too for the sake of Jacob, the angels are given to "drink" from the waters of the Great Sea, which is the Oral Torah;
וְלָכֵן נִקְרְאוּ "מַלְאֲכֵי שָׁלוֹם", וְהֵם מַלְאָכִים אַחֲרָנִין – מַלְאֲכֵי אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
. and therefore they are called "angels of peace," being a distinct group of angels—namely, the angels of the Land of Israel.

p: וְאִיתָא (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ח): בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁבָּא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִבְרוֹאת אֶת אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן נַעֲשׂוּ מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת כִּתִּים כִּתִּים
, And it is stated (in Bereishit Rabbah, Parashah 8): "When the Holy One, blessed be He, came to create Adam the First, the ministering angels formed into different factions;
מֵהֶם אוֹמְרִים אַל יִבָּרֵא וּמֵהֶם אוֹמְרִים יִבָּרֵא, הֲדָא הוּא דִכְתִיב: "חֶסֶד וֶאֱמֶת נִפְגָּשׁוּ צֶדֶק וְשָׁלוֹם נָשָׁקוּ" (תְּהִלִּים פה, יא), עַיֵּין שָׁם
. some of them said 'Let him not be created,' and some of them said 'Let him be created,' as it is written: 'Kindness and Truth met; Righteousness and Peace kissed' (Psalms 85:11)," see there.
מְפָרֵשׁ שֶׁהַמַּלְאָכִים נַעֲשׂוּ חֲבוּרוֹת, וְהַמַּלְאָכִים נִקְרְאוּ עַל שֵׁם הַמִּדּוֹת
: The Midrash explains that the angels divided into groups, each named after the divine attribute from which it stems:
מֵהֶם שֶׁל חֶסֶד – מִדַּת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ, וּמֵהֶם מַלְאֲכֵי אֱמֶת – תִּפְאֶרֶת, מִדַּת יַעֲקֹב
, some are angels of Kindness (Chesed)—the attribute of Abraham our father; some are angels of Truth (Emet)—Tiferet, the attribute of Jacob;
וּמֵהֶם שֶׁל צֶדֶק – מַלְכוּתָא קַדִּישָׁא, וּמֵהֶם שֶׁל שָׁלוֹם – מִדַּת יוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק
. some are of Righteousness (Tzedek)—holy Malchut; and some are of Peace (Shalom)—Yesod, the attribute of Joseph the Righteous.
וּכְבָר אָמַרְנוּ בְּמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב שָׁם: "נָטַל אֱמֶת וְהִשְׁלִיכוֹ לָאָרֶץ וְכוּלֵי
", And we have already noted regarding what is written there in the Midrash: "What did the Holy One, blessed be He, do? He took Truth and cast it down to the earth, etc."—
וַהֲלֹא גַּם שָׁלוֹם אָמַר אַל יִבָּרֵא דְּכוּלֵּיהּ קְטָטָה, וְלֹא נִזְכַּר מַה נַּעֲשָׂה בְּשָׁלוֹם
? why did the Midrash not mention what was done to appease the angel of Peace, seeing that Peace had also argued "Let him not be created, for he is full of strife"?
אַךְ כָּל הַקְּטָטוֹת הוּא רַק עַל יְדֵי שֶׁנֶּחְסַר מִדַּת אֱמֶת, אֲבָל כְּשֶׁכֻּלָּם מְכַוְּונִים עַל דְּבַר אֱמֶת מִמֵּילָא יֵשׁ שָׁלוֹם
, However, the answer is that all strife and contention arise only when the attribute of Truth is lacking; whereas when everyone sincerely aims for the truth, peace automatically prevails,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ בְּמַחֲלוֹקֶת בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל, שֶׁאַהֲבָה וְרֵיעוּת נוֹהֲגִין זֶה בָּזֶה לְקַיֵּים מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְהָאֱמֶת וְהַשָּׁלוֹם אֱהָבוּ", כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (יְבָמוֹת יד

:). just as we find in the disputes of Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel (in the Oral Torah), that they conducted themselves with love and friendship toward one another, fulfilling what is stated: "Love truth and peace," as taught in Yevamot (14b).
וְכֵיוָן שֶׁנָּטַל אֱמֶת וְהִשְׁלִיכוֹ לָאָרֶץ – וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁבָּאָרֶץ נִמְצָא דְּבַר אֱמֶת, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "אֱמֶת מֵאֶרֶץ תִּצְמָח" (תְּהִלִּים פה, יב

) – Therefore, once God took Truth and cast it down to the earth—meaning that within the earthly realm the Torah of truth is found and sprouts forth through human toil, as it is written: "Truth shall spring out of the earth" (Psalms 85:12)—
שׁוּב לֹא קִטְרְגוּ מַלְאֲכֵי שָׁלוֹם, דְּאַדְּרַבָּה יִהְיֶה שָׁלוֹם, דֶּאֱמֶת וְשָׁלוֹם קְשִׁיר דָּא בְּדָא
, the angels of Peace no longer objected; for on the contrary, through the Torah of truth on earth true peace is achieved, since truth and peace are bound together as one,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ בְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה: "וַיִּחַן שָׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל" – כְּאִישׁ אֶחָד בְּלֵב אֶחָד, מִיָּד "וַיֵּרֶד ה'", כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּמְּכִילְתָּא

. just as we find at the Giving of the Torah: "'And Israel encamped there' (Exodus 19:2) – as one man with one heart," whereupon immediately "Hashem descended upon Mount Sinai," as stated in the Mekhilta.

p: וְזֶה מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא לִרְבוּתָא בַּחוּרְבָּן דַּאֲפִילּוּ מַלְאֲכֵי שָׁלוֹם – שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת לְגָלוּת

, And this explains why the Gemara (Chagigah 5b) emphasized as a novelty regarding the Destruction that "even the angels of peace wept" – for these angels of the Oral Torah seemingly have no connection to exile and subjugation,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (אָבוֹת פֶּרֶק ג מִשְׁנָה ה): "כָּל הַמְקַבֵּל עָלָיו עֹל תּוֹרָה מַעֲבִירִין מִמֶּנּוּ עֹל מַלְכוּת וְכוּלֵי حکومت
", as they taught (Avot 3:5): "Whoever accepts upon himself the yoke of Torah, they remove from him the yoke of foreign , etc.," (
וּבְמִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא נֹחַ ג) וְאוֹתָן שְׁתֵּי יְשִׁיבוֹת לֹא רָאוּ שְׁבִי וְלֹא שְׁמָד וְכוּלֵי וְלֹא שָׁלַט בָּהֶם וְכוּלֵי
, (and in Midrash Tanchuma, Noach 3) that those two great academies of the Oral Torah experienced neither captivity nor forced apostasy, nor did the nations hold sway over them,
שֶׁאֵינָן בִּכְלַל גָּלוּת, שֶׁאֵין לְךָ בֶּן חוֹרִין אֶלָּא מִי שֶׁעוֹסֵק בַּתּוֹרָה
– because those immersed in the Oral Torah are not subject to exile, since "there is no free man other than one who engages in Torah" –
מִכָּל מָקוֹם גַּם מַלְאֲכֵי שָׁלוֹם בָּכוּ (בְּחוּרְבַּן אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל וּבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ
). nevertheless, at the destruction of the Temple in the Land of Israel, even the angels of peace wept bitterly.
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁאָמַר בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ דְּבָעֲקֵידָה מַלְאֲכֵי שָׁלוֹם שֶׁהֵם מַלְאֲכֵי אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל "מַר יִבְכָּיוּן
", And this is likewise what the holy Zohar stated: that at the Akeidah, the angels of peace—who are the angels of the Land of Israel—"wept bitterly,"
שֶׁכֵּיוָן שֶׁיִּשְׁחוֹט אֶת יִצְחָק אֵיךְ יֵצֵא מִמֶּנּוּ יַעֲקֹב דִּבְגִינֵיהּ אַבְטַח לוֹן שְׁלִימוּ
? fearing that if Abraham were to slaughter Isaac, how would Jacob emerge from him, for whose sake God had promised them their perfection and drink from the Oral Torah?
וְעַל שֵׁם זֶה נִקְרְאוּ בְּשֵׁם "מַלְאֲכֵי שָׁלוֹם
". And on account of this promise they are called by the name "angels of peace."

The Holy One, blessed be He, gave us a share in this completeness, as it says, “He will bless His people with peace,” and “He will grant you peace.” He therefore gave Shabbos, in which time reaches its completeness; Eretz Yisrael and the Beis HaMikdash, in which the world reaches its completeness; and the additional soul, in which souls reach their completeness. p: וּבְשַׁבָּת, דְּאִיתָא (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה יא): יַעֲקֹב שֶׁכָּתוּב בּוֹ שְׁמִירַת שַׁבָּת יָרַשׁ אֶת הָעוֹלָם שֶׁלֹּא בְּמִדָּה וְכוּלֵי
, Now regarding Shabbat, it is stated (in Bereishit Rabbah, Parashah 11; Shabbat 118b): "Jacob, concerning whom the observance of Shabbat is written, inherited the world without measure, etc.,"
וְהַיְינוּ "נַחֲלָה בְּלִי מְצָרִים" שֶׁזָּכָה כְּשֶׁהָלַךְ לְחוּץ לָאָרֶץ וְנִתְפַּחֵד
, which is the "boundless heritage" (nachalah beli metzarim) that he merited when he departed to go outside the Land of Israel and was afraid,
וְאָז הִבְטִיחוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ: "וּפָרַצְתָּ יָמָּה וָקֵדְמָה וְצָפֹנָה וָנֶגְבָּה" (בְּרֵאשִׁית כח, יד
) – whereupon Hashem, blessed be He, promised him: "And you shall spread abroad to the west, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south" (Genesis 28:14) –
שֶׁבְּכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּלֵךְ תֵּלֵךְ עִמּוֹ קְדוּשַּׁת אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
. signifying that through the sanctity of Shabbat, wherever Jacob and his descendants go, the holiness of the Land of Israel spreads and accompanies them.
וּבִכְנִיסַת שַׁבָּת אוֹמְרִים: "הַפּוֹרֵשׂ סֻכַּת שָׁלוֹם עָלֵינוּ וְעַל כָּל עַמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל וְעַל יְרוּשָׁלָיִם
", Thus, upon the entry of Shabbat we bless in the evening liturgy: "Who spreads the shelter of peace (sukkat shalom) over us, over all His people Israel, and over Jerusalem,"
וְכָל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל בְּשַׁבָּת הוּא כְּמוֹ בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל וּבִירוּשָׁלַיִם
; for on Shabbat every single Jew, even in the Diaspora, stands spiritually as though he were in the Land of Israel and in Jerusalem;
מִשּׁוּם הָכִי נִקְרָאִים הַמַּלְאָכִים בְּלֵיל שַׁבָּת "מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁלוֹם" – מַלְאֲכֵי אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, דִּבְגִינֵיהּ דְּיַעֲקֹב אַבְטַח לוֹן שְׁלִימוּ וְאִקְרוּן מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁלוֹם

. and for this reason the angels who accompany a person home on Sabbath eve are addressed as "angels of peace" (mal'akhei ha-shalom)—for they are the very angels of the Land of Israel to whom, for Jacob's sake, God promised perfection, and who are therefore called the angels of peace.
